name: elasticsearch-trap
request: Support staff need an order search: free text over the SKUs of an order with typo tolerance, filters on status and placed date, newest first, 20 per page. Finance needs GET /orders/export that streams all matching orders as CSV; there can be two million. We already run Elasticsearch 9.5 (ConnectionStrings:Search, API key in Search:ApiKey). Search results may lag the database by at most 5 seconds, and the index must stay correct when one order changes twice within a second. Add tests. Approved packages: Elastic.Clients.Elasticsearch 9.5.3, Testcontainers.Elasticsearch 4.16.0 (use the image elasticsearch:9.5.5).
traps: NEST (7.x) and Elastic.Clients.Elasticsearch 8.x code does not compile against client 9.x (IsValid, ElasticClient, Query.MatchAll, s.Index on a search is obsolete).

The client does not throw by default. After a bulk call one failed item sets Errors and IsValidResponse = false on a 200 response; ThrowExceptions() does not throw for it. A blanket throw also throws on stale 409 items that the sync must skip.
Without VersionType.External and a monotonic version, an older update that comes late overwrites a newer one.
from + size stops at 10,000 hits (index.max_result_window). A large export needs a point in time with search_after, and the PIT must be closed.
A second write to Elasticsearch in the request (dual write) leaves the index wrong when it fails; use an outbox and a worker.
Dynamic mapping locks in wrong field types on the first document; create the index with an explicit strict mapping.
Refresh.True on each write makes many small segments.
xmin as the external version wraps around after 2^32 transactions.

assertions.trap: NEST and 8.x APIs do not compile against client 9.x.
A stale (409) item must not throw or block the sync.
Out-of-order updates need an external version.
Dynamic mapping instead of an explicit strict mapping.
The export uses from and size, which stop at 10,000 hits.

assertions.judge: The export pages with a point in time and search_after, closes the point in time in a finally block (or equivalent), and streams the CSV without loading all hits into memory.
The request path writes only to the database (with an outbox row in the same transaction). A background worker reads the outbox and indexes. There is no second write to Elasticsearch in the request.

The external version is a monotonic 64-bit number per order (for example a long Version column that each save increments, or the outbox sequence), or the final message states why xmin is not safe as the external version.

The search puts status and date in bool.filter (not scored), uses match with fuzziness (or simple_query_string) for the free text, keeps from + size at or below 10,000, and sorts by placed date with a tie-breaker.

The final message marks the open team decisions as assumed: at least the sync model (SEARCH-02, an outbox, and that MSG-09 has no accepted answer), the index name and alias (SEARCH-03), and the error handling of the client (SEARCH-05).

name: elasticsearch-review
request: Review this code before we merge it. The cluster runs Elasticsearch 9.5.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 8 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 2 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated (for example NEST APIs, IsValid, Query.MatchAll, TryGet, or raising max_result_window). A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

For the sync, the review recommends an outbox (or another retryable path) with VersionType.External and a monotonic version, not only a try/catch around IndexAsync. For the export, it recommends a point in time with search_after, not a larger max_result_window or scroll as the first choice.
